answer: Pay graders with a peer-prediction rule instead of simple agreement. Each grader seals two things: its score for an answer, and its forecast of how the other graders will score it. A grader earns most when its score turns out more common than the crowd predicted, the surprisingly popular answer. Clones that share one thread of reasoning all forecast each other perfectly, so their agreement is never surprising and earns little. Moving with the tide of the panel pays less than honest private judgment, and a canyon opens between farm income and real work.
